title: University Published Paper Reproducibility Assessment Protocol
author: Scott C Edmunds
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.6x8hfrw

steps.title: Select Journals of Interest
steps.instruction: Identify journals of interest to determine the number of papers to be assigned per student using a university institutional repository (IR) or Current Research Information System (CRIS).

steps.title: Identify and Filter Papers
steps.instruction: Search for papers within the selected journals using specific filters to create a candidate list.

substeps.instruction: Filter by Journal/Proceeding/Conference (e.g., PLOS One or Scientific Reports).

steps.title: Optionally Webscrape Repository Data
steps.instruction: If the repository is built on DSpace, use the open source python script (https://github.com/jessesiu/hku_scholars_hub) to extract data.

substeps.instruction: Install BeautifulSoup bs4, urlopen, xlrd, xlwt, and csv.
Input the journal name and timeline.
Save the result file as test.txt in the current directory to obtain repository identifiers (handle, etc.), manuscript DOI, and 'Data Availability' section contents.

steps.title: Assign Papers to Students
steps.instruction: Divide and assign a suitable number of papers (e.g., 4-5 papers per student) for data availability assessment.

substeps.instruction: Paste paper details (handle/DOI/URL) into a Google Doc spreadsheet.
Instruct students to spend approximately 5-10 minutes checking each paper.
Direct students to input results into the appropriate sections of the spreadsheet.

steps.title: Assess Crowdsourced Results
steps.instruction: Review and mark the results spreadsheet completed by the students.

substeps.instruction: Double-check papers to verify the students' overall assessment of data availability.
Verify if external data sources (data DOIs or accessions, such as GeneBank accession numbers in NCBI databases) are functional.

steps.title: Verify 'Data Available on Request' Claims
steps.instruction: Test the availability of data for papers stating 'data available on request' by contacting the listed author or data access committee.

substeps.instruction: Send a simple email to the contact requesting the data (specifying de-identified/anonymised data if the nature is clinical/medical) and include the paper DOI.
Verify if the email address works and if the contact responds.
If no response is received within one week, send a second email.
If there is still no response after the second attempt, mark the data in the spreadsheet as missing.

steps.title: Calculate Final Results
steps.instruction: Use the spreadsheet data to determine the proportions of data that are available without restriction, available on request, and missing.

substeps.instruction: Assess student accuracy by comparing their data to the final assessment.
Create a corrected copy of the results with student details removed if the results are to be shared.
